==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=ICSharpCodeDecompiler&min=ICSharpCodeDecompiler&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/ICSharpCodeDecompilerTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=ICSharpCodeDecompiler&min=ICSharpCodeDecompiler&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Metadata;
using VerifyTests.ICSharpCode.Decompiler;

// Verify.ICSharpCode.Decompiler: Verifies assemblies, types, methods and properties as decompiled IL, so a change in codegen is visible.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.ICSharpCode.Decompiler
// Note: Snapshots use the .il extension, which Initialize() registers as a text extension.
// Note: Since version 3.2 the IL is normalized by default; turning that off with DontNormalizeIl()
// re-orders every existing verified file once.
// Note: The types are split across two namespaces, ICSharpCode.Decompiler.Metadata for PEFile and
// VerifyTests.ICSharpCode.Decompiler for the rest.
// Note: The package targets net48 and net8.0, so a newer project resolves the net8.0 assets.
public class ICSharpCodeDecompilerTests
{
    // The snapshot is the IL of one type, written to a .verified.il file. A change to the
    // source that does not change the IL leaves the snapshot alone, and the reverse holds too.
    [Fact]
    public async Task DecompileType()
    {
        using var file = new PEFile(AssemblyPath);
        await Verify(new TypeToDisassemble(file, "ClassBeingTested"));
    }

    // One method is usually the right size for a snapshot: a whole type re-records on every
    // unrelated edit. An overload takes a MethodDefinitionHandle for a hand picked overload.
    [Fact]
    public async Task DecompileMethod()
    {
        using var file = new PEFile(AssemblyPath);
        await Verify(new MethodToDisassemble(file, "ClassBeingTested", "FindPerson"));
    }

    // The assembly the samples decompile: the class library this solution builds. Point this
    // at whichever assembly the generated code under test ends up in.
    static string AssemblyPath => typeof(ClassBeingTested).Assembly.Location;
}
